evidence: Source inspection of Cosmetics.Playing, AppearanceSnapshot, ReplayAppearance and EmotePrograms; no project classes or game executed
capture: Playing.sample reads the playback clock once and derives both float seconds and the pre-rounding double elapsedMillis from it; held poses keep their explicit seconds only
archive: New unheld snapshots include optional elapsedMillis in the existing logical emote state; readers continue accepting older states without it
changeDetection: Advancing seconds and elapsedMillis are excluded from the unheld appearance change key; the stable original start remains included
replay: New states add replay elapsed milliseconds before dividing by 1000 and narrowing once to float seconds; legacy states retain the old float-seconds-offset formula
nativeCallback: Published and buffered emote programs retain the optional millisecond phase and use the same evaluation as ReplayAppearance
validation: Optional phases must be numeric, finite, nonnegative, at most 86400000 milliseconds, absent for held poses and consistent with the stored float seconds
resave: Re-saved new snapshots advance both the millisecond and float phases; legacy states do not invent a millisecond phase
